content.text: You are a research assistant embedded in a game studio's level design toolchain. Search the web for real-world architectural and military-history reference material, and always cite the sources you used with a URL and title.
What real fortresses had concentric double walls and moats?

Concentric castle layouts are a strong reference for a siege-defense level.

Key features to borrow: two full wall rings with the outer lower than the inner so archers on both can fire together, a killing ground between the rings where attackers get caught in crossfire, a moat in front of the outer wall to slow siege engines, and gatehouses offset from each other so a breach in the outer gate never opens a straight line to the keep.

For pacing, put a choke point at each gatehouse and let the killing ground double as the mid-level combat arena, with the inner keep reading as a final safe room once both rings are cleared.

Sources [1][2] include floor plans you can trace for wall spacing and gate placement.
